Your shipment can clear customs while the warehouse is still waiting for permission to unload the shared container. With sea freight that shares a container (LCL), your pallets stay inside until the warehouse can separate the shipments. If Australian biosecurity officers place a hold on the container during stink bug season (BMSB stands for brown marmorated stink bug), that hold can delay everyone’s freight.

If you’re waiting for your goods now, send your forwarder this message.

Can the warehouse unload the container yet? If it can, when will my shipment be ready for pickup? If it can’t, what are we waiting for and when will you update me?

November update: Where is my shipment losing time?

Check the sailing. On 4 November, Hapag-Lloyd listed individual North Asia–Australia sailings that would skip Ningbo or Qingdao to get back on schedule. If your cargo has yet to sail, ask whether it’s still booked on the original vessel. If it’s going via another port, ask if the next vessel is confirmed. Hapag-Lloyd Week 45 update

Check what’s happening after arrival. On 9 November, Australia’s agriculture department (DAFF) warned that the workload for checking documents and inspecting freight was expected to rise further before Christmas, which could affect non-urgent inspections. If your ship has arrived, ask whether the container has been unloaded from the vessel, whether a check is pending and when your own shipment can be collected. DAFF notice of 9 November

When your forwarder gives you an updated date, ask what it means. Ship arrival, cargo ready for pickup and delivery to your door are three different dates. Ask for a delivery estimate before giving your own customer a date.

Have a tracking number but still can’t find the freight? A Reddit buyer said they had a local tracking number, but the Australian delivery company could not find the shipment. In August, ABC News also reported that some RedNote users could see that their goods had arrived in Australia while they were still waiting for a clearance update. These accounts describe individual shipments. Reddit buyer discussion · ABC News reporting on RedNote posts

If your tracking has stopped updating, ask the seller or forwarder for the last confirmed location, whether the local carrier has physically received your shipment, and who will give you the next update. If they only say “customs,” ask whether they mean paperwork, a border inspection or a biosecurity check.

What if the Australian depot can no longer handle your freight?

The Top Logistics Australia (TLA) case shows how a disruption at the destination depot can leave buyers waiting for updates. In August, the Australian Border Force (ABF) announced that it had suspended depot licences in Sydney and Brisbane following an illicit tobacco investigation. ABF later told Daily Cargo News that it cancelled TLA’s licences at those two sites on 3 September and that the cancellations still stood on 27 October. The August announcement also mentioned a proposed cancellation in Melbourne. This was a customs enforcement case, separate from seasonal stink bug inspections. ABF announcement · Daily Cargo News follow-up

If your depot changes, ask your forwarder to confirm in writing where your goods are now, which depot will unload them, who is arranging the transfer and when you’ll get the next update. Keep the invoice, packing list, house bill of lading and booking confirmation together. If a charge comes through, ask for the charging party, what the charge covers, when it started and the booking term that says who pays.

What does “cleared” mean for your shipment?

Ask your customs broker what has cleared on your order. Then ask your forwarder whether the container may be unloaded. These are two separate checks. A container may be allowed to move to an inspection site while the freight inside is still unavailable for pickup. Wait for the warehouse to confirm your own shipment is ready before you send a truck.

If the forwarder says the container is on hold, ask whether it is waiting for paperwork, an inspection or pest treatment. That answer tells you whom to follow up with and what needs to happen before you can collect.

Will freight from China be checked?

Some goods shipped from China can be selected for a random check after they arrive in Australia. A shipment from China does not automatically need stink bug treatment. Ask your forwarder or broker to check your goods and the route before you book. Send the product name, where it was made and where it will ship from. Let them know if the goods will be put into a different container along the way.

For the 2026–27 season, the relevant shipping window is 1 September 2026 to 30 April 2027, inclusive. If you’re shipping close to either date, ask the forwarder to check the on-board date on the ocean bill of lading. Australian government seasonal measures

How can someone else’s goods delay yours?

Imagine your cartons share a container with a machine shipped from Italy that falls under Australia’s stink bug treatment rules. If Australian biosecurity officers order treatment on arrival, the warehouse has to wait before separating the shipments. Your cartons can be held up even when your own customs paperwork is in order.

A random inspection can work differently. At an approved site, officers may allow the container to be unloaded under inspection rules. If you’re waiting for freight, ask what the order for your container allows and whether your own goods are ready to collect. Australian government guidance on LCL containers · Checks and treatment on arrival

Questions to ask before booking

Send this table to your forwarder with your packing list and the date you need the goods.

CheckQuestion to send
Your goodsCould my goods be checked in Australia? Do they need any paperwork or treatment before shipping?
RouteWhere will my goods be packed into the shared container? Could they change containers along the way? Which vessel am I booked on?
Other goods in the containerHow do you handle cargo that needs stink bug treatment? Could it be packed with my goods?
Who to contactWhich Australian depot will unload my container? Who takes over if the depot changes, and who updates me?
Extra costsIf there is a check, treatment or extra storage, what’s included in my quote and what could I be charged separately?
PickupWho will tell me my shipment is ready? If you’re delivering it, what’s the estimated delivery date?

Send your shipment details to DDNZ on WhatsApp. Include the product, where it was made, the China pickup point, the Australian delivery postcode and the date you need it. If you’ve already booked, send your shipment reference and the latest message from your forwarder.

Common questions

Can I pick up as soon as my broker says “cleared”?

Ask the warehouse or forwarder to confirm your own shipment is ready to collect. Then book the truck.

Can the warehouse take out my pallets before treatment?

If Australian biosecurity officers require treatment of the container after arrival, the warehouse has to wait before taking out your pallets for normal delivery.

Who pays if someone else’s goods hold up my shipment?

Check your booking terms. Ask for a written breakdown of the additional costs and how any shared charges are divided.
